actor: CNA operational rules editor, CVE Program secretariat
job: Rewriting the rules that govern what a CNA may publish, so an uncorroborated report cannot leave the queue carrying a critical severity.
outcome: A published rule requiring vendor corroboration or record-keeper reproduction before a record carries a critical severity, in effect across the CNA network.
motivation: Fabricated SQLite advisories reached critical listing with nothing on the path asking whether the code they blamed existed.

task.who: CVE Board working group members and programme rule editors
task.what: Draft a corroboration precondition into the CNA rules
task.where: CVE Board working groups and the published programme rules
task.why: Nothing on the publication path checks the code exists
task.how: Public council review of a numbered rules revision

actor: Vulnerability analysis programme lead, NIST National Vulnerability Database
job: Deciding what the database does with a report the vendor has not confirmed: publish it unscored, or hold it until corroboration arrives.
outcome: A published analysis policy under which an uncorroborated record appears without a critical score rather than with one.
motivation: The database published three of the six fabricated advisories as critical, and the automation downstream reads the score rather than the record.

task.who: NVD analysis staff and programme documentation owners
task.what: Withhold the critical score until corroboration is on file
task.where: NVD analysis workflow and the public programme policy page
task.why: Automated patch cycles trigger on the score, not the text
task.how: Vendor confirmation check recorded before enrichment completes

actor: Enrichment decision owner, CISA vulnerability enrichment programme
job: Setting when the enrichment programme concurs with a submitted severity, after it concurred with all six fabricated SQLite records.
outcome: A published enrichment rule withholding concurrence with a critical severity until the affected vendor corroborates or the programme reproduces it.
motivation: The same agency's exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue carries a binding deadline only because listing there requires evidence; enrichment carries no such requirement.

task.who: CISA enrichment analysts and programme policy staff
task.what: Publish the corroboration test enrichment applies before concurring
task.where: Enrichment programme documentation and its published decision records
task.why: Concurrence is what turned a claim into a critical listing
task.how: Decision criteria modelled on the exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue's evidence bar

actor: Assignment triage lead, the CVE Program's CNA of last resort
job: Screening requests that name a project with no vendor CNA, where a submitter's claimed severity currently passes through untested.
outcome: A triage step that confirms the named function exists in the version cited before any severity leaves the queue.
motivation: The functions blamed in the six advisories did not exist in the versions named, and nobody checked before publication.

task.who: Assignment triage analysts and queue tooling maintainers
task.what: Verify the cited code exists in the named version
task.where: The assignment request queue and its triage checklist
task.why: A claimed severity currently reaches publication untested
task.how: Source lookup against the project's released tags before assignment

actor: Advisory database curation lead, GitHub Security Advisory Database
job: Deciding what an advisory published from a newly created repository has to clear before it is ingested and surfaced to dependency scanners.
outcome: Published ingest criteria under which a repository-published advisory carries no critical severity until the affected project or a curator corroborates it.
motivation: A broader audit of 55 records from that one new account found 54 fabricated; the platform is where that volume originates.

task.who: Advisory database curators and platform abuse reviewers
task.what: Hold repository-published advisories unscored pending curator corroboration
task.where: Advisory database ingest pipeline and its published curation policy
task.why: Bulk machine-generated advisories originate on the hosting platform
task.how: Curation review triggered by repository age and submission volume

actor: Vulnerability research lead, JFrog security research
job: Publishing the per-record corroboration findings behind the 55-record count, and running the same test against other accounts submitting at volume.
outcome: A public record showing this is standing throughput rather than one account, precise enough for a programme to write a rule against.
motivation: The case was caught because one company chose to look, and one audited account does not show how wide the practice runs.

task.who: JFrog security research analysts and disclosure editors
task.what: Publish the per-record corroboration findings behind the 55-record count, and the same test against other accounts submitting at volume
task.where: JFrog security research blog and its advisory write-ups
task.why: One examined project does not make a programme move
task.how: Existence and reproduction checks published per record and extended beyond one account

actor: Product security scoring lead, Red Hat Product Security
job: Reworking how a severity is assigned before publication, after the team scored a fabricated record 10.0 and later lowered it to 7.6.
outcome: A documented scoring gate requiring the cited code to be confirmed present before a severity is assigned, published alongside the rescore.
motivation: A rescore corrects one case; the vendor's own scoring practice is what other CNAs copy and what a programme rule will codify.

task.who: Red Hat product security analysts and CVSS scoring reviewers
task.what: Confirm the reported code exists before assigning severity
task.where: Product security scoring workflow and published advisory pages
task.why: A rescore fixes one record, not the practice
task.how: Pre-score existence check recorded in the advisory's scoring rationale

actor: Security response maintainer, the SQLite project
job: Publishing an authoritative, machine-readable advisory list and a dispute route, so a record-keeper has something to check a claimed SQLite flaw against.
outcome: A vendor corroboration source a programme can query automatically, making vendor confirmation a check rather than an email thread.
motivation: None of the six fabricated issues appeared on the project's own advisory page, and that absence never reached the record-keepers.

task.who: SQLite maintainers and the project's security contact
task.what: Publish advisories in a machine-readable, queryable feed
task.where: The project's advisory page and its published security contact
task.why: Absence from the vendor's own list reached nobody
task.how: Signed advisory feed in a standard vulnerability record format

actor: Remediation policy owner, an enterprise binding patch windows to CVSS bands
job: Rewriting remediation clauses and questionnaires so the patch clock starts on exploitation evidence or vendor confirmation instead of a published number.
outcome: Contract language triggering on the exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue or vendor confirmation, which is the pressure that makes restoring the severity field cheaper.
motivation: A fabricated critical spends a real patch cycle and a real change window against code that does not exist.

task.who: Vendor risk, security operations and contract owners
task.what: Retarget remediation clauses away from the published severity band
task.where: Vendor security questionnaires and remediation clauses at renewal
task.why: Clauses bound to CVSS 9.0 or above ask nothing about reality
task.how: Clause rewrite tied to the exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue at contract renewal
